messages:
alex: Hey team — customer on Private deployment (vpc-23) reports 502s when calling /v1/generate through their corp proxy. They say CONNECT opens but TLS handshake fails server-side. Sample curl from their environment:

`````
curl -v -x http://corp-proxy:8080 https://private.redwood.customer/v1/generate
* Connected to corp-proxy (10.1.2.3) port 8080 (#0)
> CONNECT private.redwood.customer:443 HTTP/1.1
< HTTP/1.1 200 Connection established
* TLSv1.2 (IN), TLS handshake, Client hello (1):
* TLSv1.2 (OUT), TLS alert, description:certificate_unknown
`````

They also pasted a gateway log line: "tls: no SNI received". Any ideas?

maria: Can you confirm proxy vendor + version? Some enterprise proxies perform SSL inspection (terminate and rewrap) and may rewrite SNI/Host or replace certs. Also confirm whether DNS resolves to an internal IP behind the proxy. If CONNECT is truly tunneled the proxy should not touch SNI.

alex: Vendor is BlueShield Proxy 6.4.0. Customer says it's in "inspection" mode and they have host-header-normalization on. They tested adding our hostname to the proxy bypass list and the requests succeed immediately. So looks like inspector is stripping SNI or doing active MITM.

jordan: If SNI is stripped the backend can't select the correct cert for the vhost — you'll see certificate_name mismatch or handshake abort. Workarounds: 1) ask proxy admin to enable TLS passthrough for private.redwood.customer (bypass SSL inspection), 2) configure proxy to preserve SNI (vendor setting), or 3) use an IP-targeted approach but our certificates are domain-based so that won't help unless we provision IP SANs (not feasible). Also capture a tcpdump on the proxy to confirm whether it performs TLS termination.

alex: They tried forcing Host header after CONNECT (curl -H 'Host: private.redwood.customer') but TLS still fails. They also added an /etc/hosts entry and used curl --connect-to <ip>:443 but the handshake still breaks — indicates the issue happens before or during SNI processing, not DNS.

maria: We can log SNI presence on our edge; eng-runtime could enable a verbose trace to confirm whether client hello contains SNI. @sam-support can we escalate for a short-term mitigation? If the proxy is resigning certs with an internal CA, that will also cause validation failures unless the proxy's CA is trusted by the client.

sam-support: Filing ENG ticket now (ENG-4137). In the meantime, advise customer to add our domain to their proxy bypass/whitelist. They confirmed bypass is allowed for this service and that fixes the flow. :white_check_mark:

opsbot: ENG-4137 created by sam-support — assigned to eng-runtime. Priority: P2. https://redwood.atlassian/ENG-4137

jordan: Quick repro steps we recommended to the customer (for their network team):
1) tcpdump on proxy for the client IP: verify CONNECT is passed through and whether proxy injects TLS data.
2) curl -v --proxy http://corp-proxy:8080 https://private.redwood.customer/v1/generate and capture raw handshake.
3) check proxy config for keywords: "SSL inspection", "splice/peek and splice", "preserve-sni", "host-header-normalization".
4) if proxy re-signs certs, ensure their client trusts the proxy CA or configure passthrough for the domain.

Also check outbound egress allowlists — some orgs have a layer that terminates and reissues certs then enforces allowlist by server CN. If the proxy returns a re-signed cert with a different CN, the client will fail validation.

maria: I'll draft a short note that support can send to the customer's proxy admin explaining cause + two short-term fixes (bypass for our domain, or change inspection to splice/preserve SNI). Alex — did they pick which path?

alex: They'll roll out bypass for a week to validate. If that works we'll close the ticket and let ENG continue with tracing. Thanks everyone.
